title: Cell attachments in the directed-union collage
statement: Use small simplicial sets and nerves from [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], and the ordered join from [lem-coef-infinity-join-cocone-associativity]. Let $K$ be a small simplicial set, $I$ a small nonempty partially ordered set, and $(K_i)_{i\in I}$ an increasing family of simplicial subsets of $K$. Let $M\subseteq K\star N(I)$ contain the pure $K$ and nerve simplices and exactly those mixed simplices $\sigma\star(i_0\leq\cdots\leq i_n)$ for which $\sigma\in K_{i_0}$. For a simplicial subset $Y\subseteq N(I)$ let $M_Y\subseteq M$ contain $K$ and those pure upper or mixed simplices whose upper block lies in $Y$. Suppose $Y'=Y\cup\tau$, where $\tau:\Delta^n\hookrightarrow N(I)$ is a nondegenerate strict chain $(i_0<\cdots<i_n)$, $n\geq1$, not in $Y$ and with $\partial\tau\subseteq Y$. Here $\partial\Delta^n\subseteq\Delta^n$ is the simplicial subset of the non-surjective monotone maps $[m]\to[n]$, $\partial\tau$ is its image under $\tau$, $Y\cup\tau$ means $Y\cup\tau(\Delta^n)$, and $N(I)^{(0)}\subseteq N(I)$ is the simplicial subset of constant chains (the vertices and their degeneracies). The natural map $K_{i_0}\star\Delta^n\to M_{Y'}$ is degreewise injective, its intersection with $M_Y$ is exactly $K_{i_0}\star\partial\Delta^n$, and the induced comparison $$M_Y\amalg_{K_{i_0}\star\partial\Delta^n}(K_{i_0}\star\Delta^n)\longrightarrow M_{Y\prime}$$ is an isomorphism of simplicial sets. At the vertex stage, $M_{N(I)^{(0)}}=K\cup\bigcup_i(K_i\star\{i\})$, and two distinct local cones intersect only in $K_i\cap K_j\subseteq K$. These assertions include empty $K$ and empty $K_i$; no directedness or covering assumption is required. Here a pushout is a colimit of the displayed span, in the sense of [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit].

source.place: Proof of Proposition 4.2.3.4, induction on the nondegenerate simplices of N(I), printed pp.249-251; explicit degreewise pushout calculation extracted for the returned step 2. Read online 2026-10-17; not archived in literature/ (WANTED).

proof.text: Use the ordered-block formula in [lem-coef-infinity-join-cocone-associativity]: in degree $m$ the pure summands are $K_m$ and $N(I)_m$, and each mixed summand has labels $(\sigma,\beta)$ with $\sigma\in K_a$, $\beta=(j_0\leq\cdots\leq j_b)$ and $a+b+1=m$. In $M$ its membership condition is $\sigma\in(K_{j_0})_a$. A simplicial operator restricts each block as specified there. If both survive, its lower label is a restriction of $\sigma$ and its upper initial vertex is some $j_t\geq j_0$; closure of $K_{j_0}$ and $K_{j_0}\subseteq K_{j_t}$ give membership. If one block disappears, the result is in a pure summand. Thus the formula indeed defines a simplicial subset $M$. Restricting the upper block to any simplicial subset $Y$ again defines a simplicial subset $M_Y$: any surviving upper block is a restriction of a simplex of $Y$, while a disappearing upper block leaves a simplex of $K$.

proof.text: Identify the image of $\tau$ with $\Delta^n$. By [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], a degree-$b$ simplex of $\Delta^n$ is a monotone map $\alpha:[b]\to[n]$. Define its boundary as the subcomplex of maps omitting a vertex: this is exactly the union of its proper faces, since a nonsurjective map factors through the face omitting any missing vertex. Every such simplex has image in $Y$ by $\partial\tau\subseteq Y$. Conversely, if $\alpha$ is surjective, choose $s(t)=\min\alpha^{-1}(t)$. Then $s:[n]\to[b]$ is monotone and $\alpha s=1$. If $\tau\alpha$ were in $Y$, restriction along $s$ would put $\tau$ in $Y$, a contradiction. Consequently $Y\cap\tau(\Delta^n)=\tau(\partial\Delta^n)$ in every degree, including all degenerate simplices.

source.place: Notation 4.2.3.1, Remark 4.2.3.2, and proof of Proposition 4.2.3.4, printed pp.248-250 (PDF pp.265-267). Agent-written ordered-block calculation expanding the asserted attachment square; read online 2026-10-17, archive WANTED.

proof.text: Put $A=K_{i_0}$, $B=A\star\Delta^n$, and $B_0=A\star\partial\Delta^n$. The map $B\to K\star N(I)$ is $A\hookrightarrow K$ on pure lower labels, $\alpha\mapsto\tau\alpha$ on pure upper labels, and $(\sigma,\alpha)\mapsto(\sigma,\tau\alpha)$ on mixed labels. It commutes with operators by the ordered-block formula of [lem-coef-infinity-join-cocone-associativity]. It is injective in each degree: block lengths are retained and both factor maps are injective, the latter because $\tau$ is an embedded strict chain. For a mixed label the first upper vertex is $i_{\alpha(0)}$, and $A\subseteq K_{i_{\alpha(0)}}$; hence its image lies in $M_{Y'}$. The pure summands do too. Denote this embedded image also by $B$.

source.place: Notation 4.2.3.1, Remark 4.2.3.2, and proof of Proposition 4.2.3.4, printed pp.248-250 (PDF pp.265-267). Agent-written ordered-block calculation expanding the asserted attachment square; read online 2026-10-17, archive WANTED.

proof.text: Compute $B\cap M_Y$ on the three types of labels. Pure lower labels are precisely $A$ on both sides. They are also the pure lower labels of $B_0$; here $n\geq1$ ensures the boundary contains vertices, and the join formula includes its pure lower summand. A pure upper label $\alpha$ lies in $M_Y$ exactly when $\tau\alpha\in Y$, which by step 2 is equivalent to $\alpha$ omitting a vertex. A mixed label $(\sigma,\alpha)$ of $B$ already satisfies the collage membership condition by step 3, so it lies in $M_Y$ exactly under the same condition $\tau\alpha\in Y$. These are exactly the pure upper and mixed labels of $B_0$. Thus $B\cap M_Y=B_0$ as simplicial subsets, not merely on vertices.

source.place: Notation 4.2.3.1, Remark 4.2.3.2, and proof of Proposition 4.2.3.4, printed pp.248-250 (PDF pp.265-267). Agent-written ordered-block calculation expanding the asserted attachment square; read online 2026-10-17, archive WANTED.

proof.text: Every simplex of $M_{Y'}$ lies in $M_Y\cup B$. This is immediate for a pure lower simplex. For a pure upper simplex outside $Y$, the equality $Y'=Y\cup\tau$ expresses it uniquely as $\tau\alpha$; by step 2, $\alpha$ is surjective, so it is in $B$. For a mixed simplex $(\sigma,\beta)$ outside $M_Y$, its upper block likewise has the form $\beta=\tau\alpha$ with $\alpha$ surjective. In particular $\alpha(0)=0$, so the initial upper vertex is $i_0$. Membership in $M$ is therefore exactly $\sigma\in K_{i_0}=A$, and this simplex is the image of $(\sigma,\alpha)\in B$. Conversely both $M_Y$ and $B$ lie in $M_{Y'}$. Hence $M_{Y'}=M_Y\cup B$ in each degree.

source.place: Notation 4.2.3.1, Remark 4.2.3.2, and proof of Proposition 4.2.3.4, printed pp.248-250 (PDF pp.265-267). Agent-written ordered-block calculation expanding the asserted attachment square; read online 2026-10-17, archive WANTED.

proof.text: Verify the pushout universal property of [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit] directly. For any simplicial set $T$ and maps $f:M_Y\to T$, $g:B\to T$ agreeing on $B_0$, define $h:M_{Y'}\to T$ on a simplex using $f$ if it lies in $M_Y$ and $g$ if it lies in $B$. Step 5 guarantees an available value; step 4 and the agreement make it independent of the choice. For any simplicial operator, choose a piece containing the original simplex. That piece is a simplicial subset, so it also contains the restricted simplex; using that same piece gives $h(\theta^*x)=\theta^*h(x)$. Thus $h$ is simplicial and has the required restrictions. The union identity makes it unique. This proves that the displayed square is a pushout. To identify its comparison with a chosen pushout $P$, glue the two canonical maps into $P$ by this construction to obtain $M_{Y'}\to P$. The composites with $P\to M_{Y'}$ restrict to the identity on both pieces and hence are identities by uniqueness. The comparison is therefore an isomorphism.

source.place: Notation 4.2.3.1, Remark 4.2.3.2, and proof of Proposition 4.2.3.4, printed pp.248-250 (PDF pp.265-267). Agent-written ordered-block calculation expanding the asserted attachment square; read online 2026-10-17, archive WANTED.

proof.text: A simplex of $N(I)^{(0)}$ is a constant chain at one vertex $i$, since the zero skeleton consists of vertices and their degeneracies. In the ordered-block formula of [lem-coef-infinity-join-cocone-associativity], the allowed mixed labels over that chain are exactly those in $K_i$; the pure upper labels are the constant chains themselves. Together with the pure $K$ labels these give $M_{N(I)^{(0)}}=K\cup\bigcup_i(K_i\star\{i\})$. For $i\ne j$, pure upper and mixed labels from the two cones cannot coincide because their upper vertices differ; the common pure lower labels are exactly $K_i\cap K_j$. If $K_i=\varnothing$, that cone still contains the vertex $i$ and its degeneracies, but no lower or mixed labels. If $K=\varnothing$, all $K_i$ are empty, $M_Y=Y$, and the square is ordinary simplex attachment along its boundary; the preceding formulas still prove it. Nothing used a common upper bound or $\bigcup_iK_i=K$: monotonicity alone was used in steps 1 and 3. Thus all stated empty cases and the absence of directedness or covering hypotheses are verified.

lean.statement: theorem infinity_local_union_cell_attachment (K : SSet.{u}) (I : Type u) [PartialOrder I] [Nonempty I] (U : I → K.Subcomplex) (hmono : Monotone U) : (∀ (Y : (nerve I).Subcomplex) (n : ℕ) (tau : (nerve I) _⦋n⦌), 1 ≤ n → StrictMono tau.obj → tau ∉ Y.obj _ → Subcomplex.range ((boundary n).ι ≫ yonedaEquiv.symm tau) ≤ Y → Mono (localUnionCell U n tau) ∧ Subcomplex.range (localUnionCell U n tau) ≤ localUnionOver U (Y ⊔ Subcomplex.ofSimplex tau) ∧ (localUnionOver U Y).preimage (localUnionCell U n tau) = Subcomplex.range (orderedJoinFunctor.map (CategoryTheory.Prod.mkHom (𝟙 (U (tau.obj 0)).toSSet) (boundary n).ι)) ∧ ∃ (h : localUnionOver U Y ≤ localUnionOver U (Y ⊔ Subcomplex.ofSimplex tau)) (top : orderedJoinFunctor.obj ((U (tau.obj 0)).toSSet, (boundary n).toSSet) ⟶ (localUnionOver U Y).toSSet) (bottom : orderedJoinFunctor.obj ((U (tau.obj 0)).toSSet, Δ[n]) ⟶ (localUnionOver U (Y ⊔ Subcomplex.ofSimplex tau)).toSSet), top ≫ (localUnionOver U Y).ι = orderedJoinFunctor.map (CategoryTheory.Prod.mkHom (𝟙 (U (tau.obj 0)).toSSet) (boundary n).ι) ≫ localUnionCell U n tau ∧ bottom ≫ (localUnionOver U (Y ⊔ Subcomplex.ofSimplex tau)).ι = localUnionCell U n tau ∧ IsPushout top (orderedJoinFunctor.map (CategoryTheory.Prod.mkHom (𝟙 (U (tau.obj 0)).toSSet) (boundary n).ι)) (Subcomplex.homOfLE h) bottom) ∧ localUnionOver U ((nerve I).skeleton 1) = Subcomplex.range (orderedJoinInl K (nerve I)) ⊔ ⨆ i : I, Subcomplex.range (localUnionCell U 0 (ComposableArrows.mk₀ i)) ∧ ∀ i j : I, i ≠ j → Subcomplex.range (localUnionCell U 0 (ComposableArrows.mk₀ i)) ⊓ Subcomplex.range (localUnionCell U 0 (ComposableArrows.mk₀ j)) = Subcomplex.range ((U i ⊓ U j).ι ≫ orderedJoinInl K (nerve I))
